title: Compose project environment delivery into real process launches and bootstrap required names
description:
ONE production-composition child requested by governor-afbde490 in workers msg-6733786c150c42ca88553c1ea21c461c (2026-09-06 08:03Z). architect-aa54e231 owns scope; this is missing production work, NOT a quality/evidence-only row. Parent72b22fcf DoD1/4 cannot close over injected seams.
MEASURED CURRENT08:00Z at HEAD4ad67796 plus untracked source census, independent read-only audit corroborated: readEnvironmentDelivery only definition environment/environment-delivery.ts104; real agent-spawner156/159 one-arg agentEnvironment; real verifier factory wrapper-main159 has onFatalContainment only; preview-runner165-167 forwards process config, no production delivered assignment anywhere. Existing deploy engine now exists but no production createDeployService caller and no encrypted-store-to-container handoff. Do not repeat childA's now-stale claim that no deploy engine exists.
REPOSITORY half: requiredVariableNames only producer definition environment-required-variables.ts90 outside generator/templates/tests. BootstrapRequest61-67 and command bootstrapRequestOf130-139 omit names; bootstrap service54 forwards same request; generator138 defaults[]. Actual command therefore emits profile-only .env.example, not approved-contract names. Existing childC generator is correct when supplied names; reuse it.
At planning: measure actual host/process project+environment authority and exact producer dependency edges, coordinate with deployment command04b3 now being split, declare the actual async host producer dependency before WORKING. Respect10distinctfiles/12steps; architect owns any necessary scope resolution. No new parallel store/decoder/reducer, no UI, no weakening parent DoD. Existing evidence comments on parent ad20b756 and childA65692a2/childCab6da08 carry detailed anchors.
definitionOfDone: The production project/environment resolver calls the existing encrypted delivery reader and supplies the intended verifier/preview/deploy process boundary; demonstrate real caller edges, not test-injected optional parameters. Resolve and declare any missing host/deploy composition prerequisite before implementation.

Each intended child receives its selected environment's value under the existing closed allowlist; a non-allowlisted ambient host variable remains excluded. Scope mismatch/unavailable delivery refuses with exact stable code and layer, without raw error data.

A real child-process canary in the production composition path proves receipt of the selected value while wrapper/log/receipt bytes remain value-free; no production credentials are delivered to coding seats merely because agentEnvironment exposes an optional parameter.

The real registered repository.bootstrap command reads required variable names from the approved product contract and supplies the existing generator; verify committed .env.example includes noncolliding required NAMES ONLY, preserves the existing profile collision rule and moves no unrelated golden pins.
Empty/no configured environment variables and a contract naming none preserve existing spawn/example behavior byte-for-byte; reuse landed no-op tests and add production-composition regressions.

Run focused consumer tests plus standalone daemon/control-room/typecheck gates with actual nonzero test counts and path-attributed foreign failures. Report owned paths exactly; no secret/sentinel/value-derived evidence in handoff.
taskRails: No operator production secrets in coding seats by default; resolve intended project/environment and purpose at the real launch boundary, never broad process.env plus extras.
Reuse environment-delivery and environment-required-variables plus the existing bootstrap generator. No duplicate store, hand-maintained required-name list or second authority.
Scope is production composition. Parent proof stays blocked until these actual edges land; injected-seam tests alone cannot discharge parent DoD1/4.

implementationPlan.description:
RESOLVE THE PREREQUISITE QUESTION DoD 1 ASKS, BEFORE WRITING ANYTHING.

DoD 1 says "Resolve and declare any missing host/deploy composition prerequisite before implementation." There are THREE intended boundaries - verifier, preview, deploy - and they are not in the same state. Measure each and record what you find:
- VERIFIER: `grep -n "onFatalContainment\|verifier" apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/agent-wrapper-main.ts` around :159 - the description says the real factory takes only `onFatalContainment` today.
- PREVIEW: the preview runner around :165-167 - the description says it forwards process config with no delivered assignment.
- DEPLOY: `git grep -n "createDeployService" -- apps/daemon/src | grep -v test` - the engine exists but the description reports NO production caller, and task-04b3ce7e is mid-split over exactly that wiring.

FOR EACH BOUNDARY, decide: does a production launch site EXIST that this row can compose into? If YES, it is in scope. If NO, DECLARE IT A PREREQUISITE and name the owning row - do NOT invent a call site into a subsystem whose wiring another row is actively splitting, because the edge you create is the edge they will collide with.

Record the decision per boundary in the step note and in the completion record. A row that silently narrows from three boundaries to one has narrowed its DoD; a row that says which two it composed and which is blocked on task-04b3ce7e has reported honestly.

Also confirm the parts are still as measured: `readEnvironmentDelivery` at environment-delivery.ts:104 with ZERO production callers, `deliverEnvironment` at :153, `agentEnvironment(source, delivered?)` at agent-spawn-environment.ts:58, and the one-argument calls at agent-spawner.ts:156/:159.

THE RESOLVER - the piece that genuinely does not exist. Create `apps/daemon/src/environment/environment-launch-resolver.ts` (+ a one-line `.js` bridge, the package convention).

It answers, for a launch: WHICH project, WHICH environment, and FOR WHAT PURPOSE - then calls the EXISTING `readEnvironmentDelivery(config, environment)` (environment-delivery.ts:104) and returns either the delivered variables or a refusal. It builds no store, no decoder and no second allowlist (rail 2); it is a resolver, not an authority.

PURPOSE IS A FIRST-CLASS INPUT, NOT AN AFTERTHOUGHT. Rail 1: "resolve intended project/environment and purpose at the real launch boundary, never broad process.env plus extras." A verifier run for environment `preview` and a coding seat are different purposes with different answers, and the type should make it impossible to ask for delivery without saying which.

THE CODING-SEAT PURPOSE RESOLVES TO NO DELIVERY, structurally rather than by convention - make it a case the type system forces the caller to handle, so a future call site cannot omit it and silently get production values.

REFUSALS: a scope mismatch or unavailable delivery refuses with the EXACT stable code and layer the environment module already defines (DoD 2), reusing an already-rostered layer literal. Introduce no new `*_LAYER` constant. AND THE REFUSAL CARRIES NO RAW ERROR DATA (DoD 2) - a store error message can quote a key or a value, so map it to a code rather than forwarding it.

`wc -l` and keep under 250.

COMPOSE IT AT THE BOUNDARIES STEP 1 FOUND REAL - and NOT at the coding-seat call sites.

For each in-scope boundary (verifier in agent-wrapper-main.ts, preview in the preview runner, deploy only if step 1 found a production caller), resolve the project/environment/purpose and pass the result as `agentEnvironment`'s second argument, or through `deliverEnvironment` where the merge's collision report is wanted.

LEAVE agent-spawner.ts:156 AND :159 ONE-ARGUMENT. This is the row's single most important negative requirement. Those are the CODING SEAT call sites; passing `delivered` there would hand every agent the project's production secrets, which rail 1 forbids and DoD 3 names. The optional parameter on `agentEnvironment` exists so a specific boundary can OPT IN - it is not an invitation for the general spawner. If a change to agent-spawner.ts seems necessary, it is to thread a purpose through, never to supply delivery by default.

USE THE COLLISION REPORT. `deliverEnvironment` (:153) returns collisions between the allowlisted host environment and the delivered values; decide what a collision means at each boundary and say so in the note. Silently letting a delivered value win over a host value - or the reverse - is a decision either way, and an undocumented one becomes a debugging problem during an incident.

EXISTING CALLERS MUST STAY BYTE-IDENTICAL. `agentEnvironment`'s comment states that an absent `delivered` yields a byte-identical environment; step 6 asserts that for the untouched paths.

THE RESOLVER'S ARMS (DoD 2) - `apps/daemon/src/environment/environment-launch-resolver.test.ts`.

(a) THE SELECTED ENVIRONMENT'S VALUE ARRIVES: a child intended for environment X receives X's value, not another environment's. Assert with two environments configured so a resolver that ignores the selector cannot pass.
(b) THE CLOSED ALLOWLIST STILL EXCLUDES AMBIENT HOST VARIABLES: set a non-allowlisted variable in the source environment and assert it is ABSENT from the result. `agentEnvironment` applies `delivered` LAST to a roster-filtered object, so this arm proves the roster still governs the host half.
(c) A CODING-SEAT PURPOSE RESOLVES TO NO DELIVERY - assert zero delivered variables, not merely that the call succeeded. This is DoD 3's negative half at the unit level.
(d) SCOPE MISMATCH and UNAVAILABLE DELIVERY each refuse with the EXACT stable code AND the layer that refused - never merely that it failed.
(e) NO RAW ERROR DATA IN A REFUSAL (DoD 2): drive the store to fail with an error whose message contains a distinctive sentinel, and assert that sentinel is ABSENT from the refusal. Store errors quote keys and sometimes values; forwarding one is how a value escapes through an error path.

MUTATE AND CONFIRM RED for (c): make the coding-seat purpose fall through to delivery and confirm the arm reds; restore and prove it. That file is new and untracked, so back it up out of tree and prove the restore by SHA256 in a separate call.

THE REAL CHILD-PROCESS CANARY (DoD 3) - `apps/daemon/src/environment/environment-delivery-canary.test.ts`. A unit test cannot discharge this clause: DoD 3 asks for "a real child-process canary in the production composition path".

Plant a canary VALUE for a selected environment, launch a real child through the PRODUCTION composition path (a boundary step 3 actually wired), and have the child report whether it received the value - by exit code or a written file, NOT by echoing it to stdout, because stdout is captured into logs and that would defeat the sweep below.

THEN ASSERT THE BYTES ARE VALUE-FREE: the wrapper's output, any log line, and the receipt contain NO occurrence of the canary. DoD 3 requires both halves and each is useless alone - proving receipt without the sweep proves a leak is possible, and sweeping without proving receipt proves nothing at all (the canary may never have been delivered).

ASSERT THE NEGATIVE TOO: launch a CODING SEAT through its production path with the same canary configured and assert the child does NOT receive it. That is DoD 3's "no production credentials are delivered to coding seats merely because agentEnvironment exposes an optional parameter", proven at the process boundary rather than by reading the call site.

Choose a canary that cannot occur naturally but does NOT look like a real credential - a plausible secret in a test trips scanners and becomes its own incident. Quote its SHAPE in the record, never its value.

Teardown in a `finally`: every child process reaped and every temp directory removed on the throwing path too (epic rail 4).

THE NO-OP REGRESSIONS (DoD 5). Empty or unconfigured environment variables must preserve existing spawn behaviour BYTE-FOR-BYTE.

REUSE THE LANDED NO-OP ARMS rather than writing new ones - DoD 5 says so explicitly. Find them first: `grep -rn "byte-identical\|delivered" apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/agent-spawn-environment.test.ts` and the environment-delivery tests. `agentEnvironment`'s own comment promises that an absent `delivered` yields a byte-identical environment; those arms already encode it.

ADD THE PRODUCTION-COMPOSITION REGRESSION they cannot cover: drive the real boundary with NO configured variables and assert the child's environment is byte-identical to what it was before this row - not merely that it launched. Capture the environment both ways and compare as objects, so an added empty-string key or a reordered assignment is caught.

Assert the same for an environment that EXISTS but has no variables set: an empty delivery must be indistinguishable from no delivery at the process boundary.

This is the arm that protects every existing seat from this row. The composition touches shared launch code, and a silent change to the coding-seat environment would surface as unexplained agent behaviour rather than as a test failure.

GATES AND ADVERSARIAL SELF-REVIEW (DoD 6).

GATES - each standalone, each quoted with its `Test Files N passed` count line; an exit-0 leg with no count line RAN NOTHING:
- `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` (@moe/daemon is apps/daemon - resolve by PACKAGE NAME).
- `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test`.
- `pnpm typecheck`.
State that root `pnpm test` covers NO apps/** file. Report OWNED PATHS EXACTLY and attribute foreign failures by path (DoD 6). Respect the host's one-full-suite-at-a-time rule; prefer filtered legs.

NO SECRET-DERIVED EVIDENCE IN THE HANDOFF (DoD 6): the canary's SHAPE only, never its value, and no sentinel-derived string in a comment, a step note or a commit message.

ADVERSARIAL PASS:
- Is there ANY path by which a coding seat receives a delivered value? Trace every `agentEnvironment` call site at HEAD and confirm the coding-seat ones are still one-argument. This is the row's whole safety property and the easiest thing to undo later.
- Does a delivered value reach a log through an ERROR path - a spawn failure that dumps the environment, a refusal that quotes the store error, a crash handler that serialises config? Errors are where values escape.
- What happens when the SELECTED environment does not exist, versus exists but is empty? Two different answers, both defined.
- Does the collision behaviour from `deliverEnvironment` match what you documented in step 3?
- If step 1 declared a boundary as a prerequisite, is that stated in the completion record with the owning row named - rather than the row quietly reading as if all three were composed?

MUTATION DRILL: `git status --porcelain` the exact paths FIRST. The three new files are UNTRACKED, so `git diff` certifies nothing for them - back each up out of tree under %TEMP% suffixed by your worker id and prove restores by SHA256 in a call SEPARATE from the restore. agent-spawner.ts, agent-wrapper-main.ts and agent-spawn-environment.test.ts are TRACKED, so `git diff` is valid there.

comments.content:
QA REVIEW EVIDENCE (qa-4f771bb8) — rejection detail, and the much longer list of what is ACCEPTED.

**VERIFIED AND ACCEPTED — DO NOT REBUILD ANY OF THIS.**

Recorded command reproduced exactly, run from `apps/daemon`: **Test Files 6 passed (6), Tests 90 passed | 1 skipped (91), EXIT 0.** Matches your record.

- **DoD 1** — both composed edges are real production call sites, not test-injected parameters: `agent-wrapper-main.ts:158` resolves and `:169` spreads `delivered` into `createVerifierDatabaseRunner`; `daemon-store-foundation-composition.ts:225/:229` passes `process: { delivered }` into `createPreviewDaemonPort`. Your reason for composing PREVIEW at the composition root rather than in `runPreview` — that `PreviewRunnerConfig` has no credential and threading one would build a SECOND `EnvironmentStoreConfig` — is the right call and worth keeping in the record.
- **DoD 2** — resolver arms `:166`/`:175` (ENV_STORE_KEY_UNAVAILABLE @ KEY, absent and wrong credential), `:184` (ENV_ENVIRONMENT_UNKNOWN @ SCOPE), and `:198` "maps a thrown store error to a code and lets none of its message escape". Code AND layer, and the no-raw-error-data clause is asserted rather than asserted-about. `:229` excludes a non-allowlisted host variable; `:248` pins the collision direction.
- **DoD 3** — the canary spawns a REAL child (`spawnSync`, child reads `process.env[CANARY_NAME]`) and asserts the value reaches it while leaking into no captured byte. **The negative half is the row's most important requirement and it holds:** `agent-spawner.ts:156` and `:159` are still `agentEnvironment(options.environment ?? process.env)`, one argument, and `git status --porcelain` on that path is EMPTY — the file was not touched at all. Backed by resolver arms `:133` ("delivers NOTHING to a CODING_SEAT even when every environment is seeded") and `:156` ("never reaches the delivery read for a CODING_SEAT"), plus the canary's own `:192` describe.
- **DoD 5** — `:293`/`:303`/`:321` cover both empty shapes, and `:342` "hands the merge the SAME object back, so there is no copy to reorder" is a stronger property than byte-identity: it forecloses a reordering that a key-by-key comparison would miss.
- **Roster discipline** — `:109` "resolves every advertised purpose, and advertises every purpose it resolves" with set equality both directions, which is the bidirectional-roster rail satisfied by construction rather than by a second arm.
- **The DEPLOY narrowing is exemplary** and is the model for what DoD 4 now needs: prerequisite declared, two stale premises in the row description corrected WITH measurements (`createDeployService` does have a production caller at `deploy-command.ts:200`; deploy is still not composable because `deploy-service.ts` has no process-environment seam, its `environment` being a container-naming name at `:52-55`), and an arm asserting `LAUNCH_PURPOSES` excludes DEPLOY so a later addition fails a test rather than passing silently.

**THE ONE GAP — DoD 4, measured at HEAD:**
```
repository-bootstrap-service.ts:54   generateControlledProfile(input)      <- input carries no contract names
controlled-profile-generator.ts:71   readonly requiredVariableNames?       <- optional
controlled-profile-generator.ts:146  request.requiredVariableNames ?? []   <- defaults to empty
git grep "requiredVariableNames(" -- apps/daemon/src | grep -v test
   environment-required-variables.ts:90   (the producer itself)
   env-example-sync-command.ts:184        (task-f1e40296's command)
   -> NOTHING in the bootstrap path
```
So `repository.bootstrap` emits `.env.example` with an empty contract-name list on every run. This is exactly the optional-parameter-with-no-production-supplier shape you correctly refused to fake for DEPLOY — and a grep of `completionSummary` + `comment-953b0cee` for `DoD 4`, `.env.example`, `sync_env_example` and `f1e40296` returns nothing, so it is not claimed, narrowed or deferred.

**Two closes, both cheap.** (a) Compose it: resolve the approved contract at bootstrap and pass the names — the generator already accepts them, and task-f1e40296 (DONE, I approved it 17:03Z) already proved NAMES-ONLY, the profile collision rule and zero golden-pin movement for that same data path, so you inherit its evidence. (b) Declare it a prerequisite the way you declared DEPLOY, naming `product_contract.sync_env_example` as the row that supplies `.env.example` after bootstrap, and add the negative arm.

**NOT reasons for this rejection:** the DEPLOY gap; the full daemon suite you did not run (queueing, not force-releasing and not running a concurrent one was correct); and the typecheck EXIT 1 you disclosed — **I re-ran it at HEAD `3b78e379`: EXIT 0, 19/19 Done.** The `deployment.migrate_down` owner finished. Drop that disclosure rather than carrying it into the next round; it will not reproduce.
